questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to go to a destination where I could feel at home. It was a goal for me to make Amsterdam my second home for the future by getting to know the city, the people and the culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It took a lot of effort to complete everything before going, but it was all worth it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was not too hard to find information about the university and housing, but I think it is also a matter of being okay with not knowing everything before arrival, but trust that you will get information when needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The people from DUWO helped me with getting my room and the university was given me information about the introduction week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not get invitations for master student events, because I have been on Erasmus, which could have been nice since it was those people I have been studying with. Luckily I got invited to the pub quiz by someone from my course and got in because I few people did not show up.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We have a kitchen, but it is not really well equipped and do not have an oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is really nice and you get to know a lot of people because you live at the same place. It is easy to meet up and I got close friendships with people from my campus housing, because we were able to meet for dinner on Sundays etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard to get a place and to know what to look for, but I am so happy for were I ended up.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was easy because it could all be done online, but finding courses was hard.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was really hard finding the courses that I could actually sign up for and it seems that there some courses available for some people and others for other people. I found it difficult to know if a course is a bachelor or master course and if it was available for me to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email the incoming exchange team. There were really helpful and answered quick always.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found some good classes which I have been happy for. Although, some of them were not as relevant as I thought they would have been.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Accept that you need to spend time looking at it and ask for help if something is unclear. Be open to the courses and expect that they are different from what you might think.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The psychology programme I followed was really meaningful and I learned a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level good. It was not hard to follow, but still I needed to put in some effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical, which I really liked.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Psychopathology (P1+2)
Sensemaking in Organizations (P1)
Transnational Organizations in a Global World (P2)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Psychopathology: because it gave a great understanding of different psychopathology and also focused on academic writing. 
Sensemaking in Organizations: because it was different from what I tried before and opened my mind for new perspectives on the world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used public transportation more than I thought I would. I did not think about all the things I had to buy in the beginning like a kettle, laundry rack, towels, some kitchen stuff etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Renting a bike (Swapfiets) was less expensive, we could get almost all our books online for free for uni. Being social in general were more expensive than I though because you do not have the same opportunities to cook for friends at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of opportunities for sport and trying new things. Also the university has a nice cinema!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym, volleyball fields, cinema.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The cinema. The most important thing is to attend the events that is organized in the introduction week, because it is here you meet the people that you will spend the rest of your time with. I was a part of a free running club called Running Junkies which was really nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get a museum card and go to a lot of museums. Go to the flea market in North in the IJ-hallen. Albert Cuyp market. Vondelpark and Westerpark. Go to the cities around Amsterdam, especially go to Haag, Haarlem and Rotterdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. The Dutch people are really nice and everyone speaks English, even old people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do not think too much about talking English, because they also do not care.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biking culture. It is also fun, you just need to be aware all the time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate that Dutch people are really direct and also that the are good at being on time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: (1) Participate in the introduction week. (2) Remember to get rest and do not feel bad about missing a party or another social event - you will not loose any friends and it is important to recover sometimes. (3) Enjoy the time, and do not stress about seeing everything in the city. A beer in a local café with friends can be even better than spending a few hours at a big turist attraction or in club.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dutch weather can be hard, so bring rain clothes and warm sweaters.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot about friendship in general, but by getting a lot of new friends and by being in contact and also missing the friends I have back at home. I learned things about myself by allowing me to not always act in the way I think I should, but to actually do what I wanted in the moment. Being spontaneous and trusting that things will work out in the end was also a big part of what I learned.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling alone sometimes. Even surrounded by nice people you might not get the same that from you friends back home because everyone is still new friends. Everyone feels exactly this though, so if you dare speak to your new friends about it, your friends can probably grow even stronger.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Be brave to share how you are and feel about being abroad with new friends. They probably feel exactly the same way and this makes it way easier when things with university is hard or something happens back home, because then you can support each other.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
